reading.body:
Data Foundry Austin 1 occupies 40,000 square feet of technical space in Travis County, Texas. The operator has not published a power figure for this facility, so no IT load, critical load, or UPS capacity is on record here. Without a megawatt number, no rack-count or accelerator estimate can be responsibly derived.

The absence of a published power figure also places this campus outside the 13 Texas facilities for which this site holds capacity data, meaning it does not contribute to the 389 MW total mapped across the state. The state context ranks it 14th by published megawatts, but that ranking reflects the absence of a figure rather than a measured position, because any facility without a published number sorts below all 13 that have one. Texas has 133 mapped facilities in total, and the majority of those publish no power specification, so Austin 1 is typical of the state in that regard.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI workloads, the 40,000 square feet of technical space signals a mid-sized colocation facility rather than a hyperscale build, but floor area alone does not determine AI suitability. Power density per rack and total available power are the constraints that govern whether a site can support GPU clusters, and neither figure is published here. Until the operator publishes a power specification, this campus cannot be evaluated against the grid-constrained scaling thesis that defines AI infrastructure relevance.
